title: Exact cocycle and twisted-boundary verification for Family 199
description:
Independent exact verification of a finite algebraic interface in OpenAI mathematics Family 199, the proposed Auslander–Reiten counterexample. The explicit 179-entry degree-three cochain satisfies its Hochschild cocycle identity on all 104,976 radical basis quadruples and its twisted boundary identity on all 324 pairs, with q and invertible H symbolic. The displayed bar cycle has zero differential and evaluates to q³, which is nonzero over the source field F₂(q,H₁,H₂).

The main implementation derives the twenty-dimensional trivial extension from the ten-dimensional starting algebra and computes over F₂[q,H,H⁻¹]. A separately tasked AI reviewer independently retranscribed the source and supplied a second implementation using binary polynomial coefficients and accumulation of nonzero differential terms. Both complete finite checks pass. Additional checks cover all 8,000 associativity triples, 400 trace-duality pairs, 22 unit/integration tests and deliberately corrupted coefficients, dual products and twists. Positive and rejection checks run under ordinary and optimized Python. The missing-twist control produces q(1+H)z, illustrating a defect that specialization at H=1 would miss.

The source already supplies these identities and finite recurrences. This contribution adds independent verification beyond Pico’s earlier starting-algebra check; it is not a new counterexample or a missing-proof allegation. The extension from basis computations uses a written multilinearity argument; interpretation of the nonzero class uses the standard relative-bar resolution after extension to the source field. The later explicit resolution, all-degree Ext vanishing, cone/lift steps, Tachikawa analogue and full Auslander–Reiten counterexample are outside scope. There is no kernel verification or human peer-review claim.

The self-contained archive freezes public contribution 9ce7229089c23e26630850b3c7165a77e9297b85, with source snapshots and hashes, both implementations, tests, controls, written scope note, independent AI review, outputs and licenses. OpenAI supplied the mathematics and table; Pico, operated by Håkon Åmdal, supplied the predecessor algebra verification. Alexander Richard Towell contributed with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in implementation, checking, exposition, packaging and review.
